result: h07. **Where the URL comes from:** the browser never gets raw avatar bytes in the user JSON — `convertUserFromStore` rewrites a base64 data-URI avatar into the path `/file/users/{username}/avatar` (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:31-39`, name built by `BuildUserName` at `server/router/api/v1/user_resource_name.go:13`). `` puts that into an `` (`web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14`), so the browser issues a plain GET. Request path from that GET down to stored data: ``` — web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14 FileServerService.RegisterRoutes (GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121 (wired at server/server.go:81-82) FileServerService.serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 FileServerService.getCurrentUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 [only when !Profile.AllowAnonymous()] Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser — server/auth/authenticator.go:190 [same conditional branch] FileServerService.getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148 [userCache hit only when find.ID set; username lookup always falls through] Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:136 Driver.ListUsers (interface) — store/driver.go:47 DB.ListUsers (SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (also store/db/postgres/user.go:87, store/db/mysql/user.go:84) FileServerService.parseDataURI (base64-decode store.User.AvatarURL) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737 c.Blob(200, imageType, imageData) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:203 ``` Two notes worth flagging: - The avatar bytes live **in the `user.avatar_url` column as a base64 data URI**, not in object/file storage. So the "data layer" hop terminates at the SQL row — there is no local-disk or S3 branch here, unlike `serveAttachmentFile`, which fans out to `resolveLocalPath`/`getAttachmentReader`/S3 (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:126-190`). - The handler resolves the target user by **username only** (`store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}`), and authorization is coarse: on a public instance (`Profile.AllowAnonymous()`) any visitor gets any user's avatar; on a private instance any authenticated viewer does. There's no per-user check tying the viewer to the requested profile.
